title: Smart waste sorting and bin monitoring
intro: A frozen MobileNetV3-small feature extractor and a trained linear classifier recognize cardboard, glass, metal, paper and plastic. Confidence rejection, mixed-material flags and bin checks can route an item to review. A disposal is counted only after actuator acknowledgement; jams, stale sensors and timeouts stop the simulated mechanism.
scope: Raspberry Pi targeted, desktop simulation tested. No Pi, real sensor, electrical power, camera timing, motor or physical safety validation was performed. This is an AI-assisted personal engineering project; it does not establish professional seniority or independent authorship.
policies: IDLE accepts a new item only with valid five-class probabilities, configured confidence and margin, and healthy capacity sensors.
Unknown, mixed or full-bin inputs enter REVIEW. Fill >=90% or weight >=2000 g inhibits routing.
MOVING counts exactly once on acknowledgement. Virtual acknowledgement occurs after one simulated second; manual acknowledgement is also available.
Jam, invalid sensors, capacity becoming full, or a three-second timeout enters FAULT before acknowledgement. Reset returns to REVIEW. Restart never automatically resumes motion.
model: Training used 1457 known-class images, 478 known validation images and 452 known test images. Unknown-proxy trash counts are 39 validation and 21 test; 77 train-bucket trash images were unused. SHA256 groups exact duplicates into fixed roughly 60/20/20 buckets. A 576-feature frozen ImageNet MobileNetV3-small backbone feeds StandardScaler and balanced L2 multinomial logistic regression. Only the scaler and linear head were fitted on training data. C in {0.01, 0.1, 1} and rejection settings were selected on validation. Frozen C=0.01, threshold=0.5, margin=0.0. No CNN fine-tuning or training from scratch occurred.
tradeoff: Known-class accuracy rose from 62.17% to 90.27%, a 28.10 percentage-point gain (45.20% relative). The feature extractor costs more computation than a color histogram. The selected rejection rule recognized only 4 of 21 unknown-proxy images, or 19.05%. A confident prediction cannot establish purity or suitability for automatic disposal.
limitations: TrashNet contains mostly isolated objects and is not representative of dirty mixed waste streams. Exact duplicates are grouped, but physical-object/session identifiers are unavailable, so near-duplicate leakage cannot be excluded. Trash is a narrow proxy for unfamiliar items. In 60 mixed-image composites, only 16 were rejected. Dirt, resampling and black masks are synthetic stress probes, not physical crushing, dirt or hidden contamination measurements.

demo: Choose paper and Run AI on sample. Sort latest AI result then advance one second to count acknowledgement. Click unknown to route scripted uncertainty to REVIEW; full to inhibit sorting; jam to enter FAULT. Restore devices and Clear fault to return to review; a new item requires a new decision.
bom: Raspberry Pi 4 or 5, USB camera and fixed illumination, small bench servo, distance sensor for fill, load cell with a calibrated USB serial bridge, position/limit switch and jam input, separate regulated servo supply.
wiring: Example BCM allocation: fill trigger GPIO23 and echo GPIO24 through suitable level conversion; servo signal GPIO18; jam input GPIO17; position acknowledgement GPIO27. Weight readings arrive on a USB serial bridge at 115200 baud as one calibrated gram value per line. Direct HX711 support is not implemented.
resume: Trained a five-class waste classifier using frozen MobileNetV3 features and a balanced linear head on 1457 training images, with separate validation and test splits.
Raised held-out known-material accuracy from 62.17% to 90.27% on 452 images against a color-feature baseline; reported unknown rejection separately at 4/21.
Implemented acknowledged sorting, duplicate-event handling and full-bin, jam and timeout recovery; eliminated 50 unsafe disposals in a 60-case scripted comparison.
